answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it earns voting weight or access to shared rewards. Splitting one stake across a hundred accounts does not create more influence, while each account adds setup and monitoring overhead; attacking at scale therefore ties up capital that could otherwise earn returns. A trust score based only on activity is hollow, an ivory badge proves little, and a fable of effortless identities fails when influence is stake-limited.
